AWARD DATED:
22.6.2013 PASSED IN MVC NO.7661/2011 ON THE FILE OF THE 7TH ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE, MEMBER, MACT- 3, BANGALORE, AWARDING A COMPENSATION OF RS.5,92,500/- WITH INTEREST @ 8% P.A.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

These two appeals are preferred by the owner of the offending vehicle being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore dated 22.06.2013 in MVC Nos.7660 and 7661 of 2011.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are:
On 29.10.2011 at about 06.30 p.m., the claimants were proceeding on a motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA-08/J- 4216 and when they were near Varadapuar gate,
Petrol Tanker Lorry bearing registration No.KA-02/AB-3006 dashed against the claimants vehicle, due to which they fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
4.
Immediately after the accident, the claimants were shifted to M.V.J. Hospital, Hosakote and thereafter, they were shifted to Axon Speciality Hospital, where they were inpatient.
It is the case of the claimants that they spent huge sums towards their treatment.

5. It is stated that prior to occurrence of accident, the claimant, in MVC No.7660/2011, was hale and healthy, aged about 22 years and was working as a Maintenance Engineer in Ferrum Extreme Engineering, Industrial Area, Hosakote and the claimant, in MVC No.766/2011, was hale and A. Karthikeyan vs Baliram Yadav on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111735090/
3 healthy, aged about 25 years and was earning Rs.9,000/- per month by doing agriculture.
Due to the occurrence of accident, the claimants have expended huge amount towards medical expenses and incidental expenses and have sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Hence, they filed a claim petitions before the Tribunal seeking compensation.
6. On service of notice, respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle and respondent No.2-insurance company filed their respective written statement contending that the claim petitions are not maintainable.
Respondent No.1 - Owner of the while admitting the ownership of the vehicle contended that, the vehicle has been insured with respondent No.2.

Respondent No.2 while denying the existence of insurance issued in respect of Petrol Tanker Lorry registration No.KA-02/AB-3006 restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy and the driver of the Petrol Tanker Lorry did not possess valid driving licence and thereby, owner has violated that policy conditions.
It also denied the age, avocation and income of the claimants and contended that the claim petitions are excessive and exorbitant.
All other allegations made in the claim petitions were denied by the respondent.
7. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

8. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimants got examined themselves as PW1 and PW2 and also examined PW3 - Doctor in support of their case and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P213.

On the other hand, respondent No.2-Insurance Company examined one witness as RW.1 and respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle got examined himself as RW2 and got marked documents Exs.R1 to R8.
9.

On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary, the Tribunal awarded the compensation in a sum of Rs.11,27,740/- in MVC No.7660/2011 and Rs.5,92,500/- in MVC No.7661/2011 with interest at the rate of 8% per annum and respondent No.1 - owner of the vehicle was fastened with the liability and was directed to pay the entire compensation amount to the claimants and the claim petitions against the insurance company, who being respondent No.2 before the Tribunal, came to be dismissed.
Aggrieved by which, the owner of the offending vehicle is before this Court.

10. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant-owner of the offending vehicle and the learned counsel for the claimants that MFA Nos.8193 and 8194 of 2013 filed by the claimants were referred to Lok-Adalat and the matters were settled before the Lok-Adalat on 13.08.2022.

11. In the said appeals preferred by the claimants being aggrieved by the very same impugned judgment and award, the insurance company, who was also party to the proceedings having participated before the Lok-Adalat, amicably settled the dispute and the insurance company by accepting the liability has satisfied the entire award in favour of the claimants.

12. In view of the same, the present appeals preferred by the owner of the offending vehicle with regard to the liability fastened on him has been settled and accepted by the insurance company in the aforementioned appeals.
